title: Trumpeters' envy and Armstrong's influence on black trumpet players
summary: Barker says trumpet players everywhere were overshadowed by Armstrong, and many built styles on his recorded solos while many whites preferred Bix.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: So, he scowled at me, he said, so your sons of bitches take, you son of, some son of bitches, he said, take too many liberties with people. He was mad because lawyer had played, see? I don't think it was so much about the horn. And, I used to know his name, I can't think of his name. He was one of those supposed to be hot trumpet players, right? She called him. Guys who were celebrated in their hometown as being great trumpet players after lawyer came through there, playing like, you know, playing that big, beautiful tone, playing so beautiful. And, Lala, if you caught him, if you're in a mood and you play Tiger Rag or Chinatown, 50, 60 choruses, you know, wiping his chops with that handker and blowing, exhilarating excitement the way he could, well, most trumpet players, they couldn't take it. They professed that, they loved it, but deep down inside, you know, they couldn't come up with that thing, see?
Do you think, do you think that it bothered most of them that he was that good or do you think they really felt a legitimate warmth and passion for the way he played?

A lot of them had a passion and not, he was such a dominant figuring on trumpet playing, particularly amongst black musicians and white, and then white, but amongst blacks, ones who had, who, who, who, who, who could absorb the soul of what he played and had been around, exposed to the lifestyle he had, could relate to what he was playing and, and a whole slew of, of trumpet players, black trumpet players, received some acclaim by even just playing his solos. It ain't, maybe not to the same perfection, but just playing his solos off of records and if you could learn to play, say, a dozen or so of Lewis, great, exceptionally great solos and adopted, you had a style there, which was international style acclaimed by everybody. so you wasn't, you was in business if you just could play.
